## Objective

Get the project running on your machine, with your own keys, and prove it works
before spending any quota.

## Why this step exists

Most "it doesn't work" problems in a workshop are environment problems, not code
problems. We front-load them and give you a single command that proves the whole
setup is sound.

## Get the code

```bash
git clone https://github.com/dileepadev/deploying-agentic-ai-apps-workshop.git
cd deploying-agentic-ai-apps-workshop
```

## Install uv

[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) manages the Python version, the virtual
environment, and the packages — one tool instead of four.

<Tabs>
<TabItem label="macOS / Linux">


```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Windows">


```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Already have pipx or brew">


```bash
brew install uv        # or:  pipx install uv
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Then:

```bash
uv sync
```

That reads `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, installs the exact versions this
project was tested with, and creates `.venv` for you. **You never need to
activate it** — `uv run` handles that.

## Configure your secrets

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

Open `.env` and fill in three values:

| Variable | Where to get it |
|---|---|
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | [https://aistudio.google.com/apikey](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) → *Create API key* |
| `SUPABASE_URL` | Supabase → Project Settings → API → *Project URL* |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | same page, the **service_role** key |

<Aside type="danger" title="The service_role key bypasses every database security rule">


It belongs on your server and nowhere else. Never in frontend code, a
screenshot, a commit, or a chat message.

`.env` is already in `.gitignore` — check that it stays there. Once a key is
pushed to GitHub it is in the history forever and must be rotated.

</Aside>

## Prove it works

Run the tests. They need **no API key and no network**:

```bash
uv run --extra dev pytest
```

```text
............                                        [100%]
12 passed
```

Then start the server:

```bash
uv run fastapi dev app/main.py
```

## Expected result

Open [http://localhost:8000/health](http://localhost:8000/health). You want:

```json
{"ok": true, "database": true, "model": "gemini-flash-latest"}
```

Also open [http://localhost:8000/docs](http://localhost:8000/docs) — FastAPI generates that from your code,
and you'll use it to test the deployed version later.

## What usually goes wrong

<details>
<summary><code>database: false</code></summary>


Your `SUPABASE_URL` or key is wrong, or the project is paused. Free projects
pause after about a week idle — open the Supabase dashboard and resume it.

You haven't created the tables yet either — that's [step 2](../02-database/).
`database: false` at this point is expected if you've skipped ahead.

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>RuntimeError: Missing environment variable: GEMINI_API_KEY</code></summary>


Working as intended — config fails loudly at startup rather than mysteriously
at request time. Check `.env` exists in the **repo root**, not in `app/`, and
that there are no quotes around the values.

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>uv: command not found</code> after installing</summary>


The installer added it to a shell profile that your current terminal hasn't
read. Open a new terminal, or `source ~/.bashrc` / `source ~/.zshrc`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Python version errors</summary>


You don't need to fix your system Python. `uv python install 3.12` then
`uv sync` again — uv will use its own.

</details>

## What's next

You have an environment. Now it needs somewhere to put things.
